presentation_question: Is the cliff only a Chrome EventDispatch accounting artifact?
what_is_closed: Key-held 1000ms drops persist through editor input, second RAF, Paint, DrawFrame, first changed trace screenshot, and localized changed pixels.
remaining_caveat: These endpoints are still browser-derived and not an external display measurement.
calibration_contract: No new calibration is needed for this internal-browser claim; keep reporting it as Chromium visual/render endpoint evidence, not hardware-to-screen latency.

presentation_question: Is the changed trace screenshot unrelated to the typed character?
what_is_closed: Every decoded retained pixel-localization sample overlaps the target textbox and the typed x range in both input modes at 990ms, 1000ms, and 1300ms.
remaining_caveat: Pixel overlap is not OCR and does not semantically prove the glyph a user perceived.
calibration_contract: An OCR or image-recognition pass should crop the DOM range, require recognition of the newly inserted glyph, and report first recognized-glyph timestamp against the same keydown/EventDispatch window.

presentation_question: Is post-EventDispatch rendering the main visual cliff?
what_is_closed: Paint and DrawFrame endpoint drops are about 12ms with only 0.2-0.8ms post-EventDispatch tail movement; first changed screenshots have a larger 2.3ms tail but still mostly follow EventDispatch.
remaining_caveat: A calibrated presentation pipeline could add compositor/display tail that these traces do not measure.
calibration_contract: Compositor/presentation tracing should decompose keydown to EventDispatch, Paint/DrawFrame, compositor submit, swap/present, and screenshot/camera-visible glyph for the same retained samples.

presentation_question: Can trace screenshots be treated as screen presentation timestamps?
what_is_closed: Trace screenshots preserve the key-held shape and localize the changed pixels, but they are Chromium trace artifacts with endpoint-specific offsets.
remaining_caveat: Actual display presentation, scanout, compositor buffering, and panel timing are unmeasured.
calibration_contract: Run compositor presentation traces or high-speed camera capture on the same 990ms, 1000ms, and 1300ms key-held and complete-keypress controls; success requires the 1000ms key-held drop to persist at first presented or first camera-visible glyph.

presentation_question: What can CI claim without external calibration?
current_local_answer: That the held-key artifact propagates to Chromium internal visual endpoints, not that a user saw the glyph at that exact timestamp.
what_is_closed: The complete-keypress-then-wait control stays flat while the held-key mode moves across multiple internal visual endpoints.
remaining_caveat: Hardware-to-screen latency and semantic first-visible-glyph timing remain outside the current evidence.
calibration_contract: Keep CI/report language scoped to EventDispatch, render trace, and localized trace-screenshot endpoints unless an external presentation/OCR calibration is added.
